blocks.text:
Amy Alvarez
General Manager
Howard, Carlson and Tran
Dear Amy,

Thank you for choosing us to find your next General Counsel. This letter sets out how we will run that search for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}, and the terms we will run it under. We treat a retained mandate as a partnership. So we like to begin with everything said plainly, in writing, before the work starts. Please read what follows with care. If any line does not match what we agreed, call me before you sign, and we will put it right.
The Search Before Us

You need a General Counsel who can be a true partner to your leadership, not only a careful lawyer. Our task is to find that person, to test them hard, and to bring you a short slate you can act on with confidence. We work on a retained basis. That means we work for you alone on this search, and we stay with it until the seat is filled. Discretion runs through all of it. We describe prospective candidates to you by their current role and record, never by name in anything that circulates, and we hold names close until both sides are ready to meet.
The assignment moves through a few clear stages, and I want you to know the shape of it from the first day.

items: First, we agree the position specification with you and your board, so we are all searching for the same person.
Second, we map the market, build a long list from that map, and approach prospects with care.
Third, we interview and assess in depth, then bring you a short slate framed by fit and evidence, not by name alone.
Fourth, we stay beside you through your own interviews, the references, and the offer, and we do not step back until your new General Counsel has accepted and started.

blocks.text: Who Will Do the Work

I will oversee this engagement myself, and I remain your point of contact whenever you want one. Sandra Fuentes, a Principal in our practice, will lead the search day to day and own the relationship with you and with every candidate she brings forward. James Grant, also a Principal, will work the most senior end of the market and lend his judgment on the finalists. Nicole Donovan, our Research Associate, will build the candidate research and keep the small loops closed, so nothing on our side goes quiet on you. You will find us easy to reach.
Our Fee, and When We Start

For a retained search of this kind we work to a fixed professional fee of {{fact:f:E-2019-001.fee}}. That fee covers the whole assignment, from the specification through to a placement made. It is not tied to the pay of the person you hire. You know the cost at the outset, and it does not move as the search does. We are ready to begin on {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}, once this letter is signed and returned, and we will hold that date for you.
How We Invoice

We bill the fixed fee in three parts, tied to the milestones of the search: at your signing of this letter, at the delivery of the short slate, and on your chosen candidate's acceptance. Invoices are due on receipt. Reasonable direct costs that we arrange at your request, such as candidate travel, are billed at cost and shown in full. We will clear anything out of the ordinary with you first.
The Length of the Engagement, and Ending It

The engagement runs from your signature until the search is done and our final invoice is settled. Either of us may end it sooner, in writing. We ask only for a short conversation first, so nothing ends on a misunderstanding. If you close the search early for a reason unrelated to our work, we bill for the stage in hand and no further. If a General Counsel we place leaves you within the first year for reasons within our control, we will reopen the search once at no added fee.
Holding Confidence

We treat what you tell us, and all we learn during the search, as confidential, and we use it only for this work. Inside our office, access sits with the people named above and with those whose work on the search requires it. We extend the same care to candidates. We do not reveal a prospect's interest to anyone outside your committee without their knowledge, and we describe them by their role rather than their name until you are ready to meet. We guard that discretion closely, because it is the reason strong candidates are willing to speak with us while they are still in post.
Where Our Liability Sits

We give this search our best professional judgment. Still, the choice of whom to hire is finally yours, and we cannot warrant how any person will perform once appointed. Our liability to you under this engagement, whether framed in contract or in negligence, will not exceed the total fees you pay us under it, save for our own fraud or willful misconduct. Neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss.
The Law That Governs Us

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our office sits, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Should any dispute arise, we will each make a real effort to settle it in conversation before either of us turns elsewhere.

If these terms read as we agreed, the next step is a simple one. Please sign both copies where shown below, keep one for your file, and return the other to me. That single signature is all we need to begin. If anything here gives you pause, call me first, and we will settle it before you sign. We are glad to be doing this with you.
With warm regards,
Kickoff Memo: General Counsel Search for Howard, Carlson and Tran

To: Sandra Fuentes; James Grant
From: Nicole Donovan
Re: How we will run the General Counsel search

Our objective is a single one, and it should govern every choice from here: place a General Counsel with {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} whom their board will still be glad to have hired three years on. We agreed the mandate with the client's General Manager, Amy Alvarez, and the engagement begins on {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}. This memo records the plan we set at kickoff, so the three of us work from one brief rather than three. The search will run heavily on correspondence, because the strongest candidates are not looking and both sides will need steady contact to stay comfortable.
The role we are filling

The client wants a General Counsel who is a genuine partner to leadership, not only a technical lawyer. They have said little yet about the finer points of the brief, which is why the specification comes first. Settling it with Amy Alvarez and her board is the first real task on the account, and it will set the terms every later decision rests on. The profile we build from it should read the same to all three of us, so that the field we assemble answers one brief and not three private readings of it. Discretion holds throughout: we describe candidates by their current seat and record, and we hold names until both sides want to meet.
How the work divides

items: Specification: Sandra Fuentes drafts the position specification and settles it with the client, so the whole team searches against one agreed brief rather than four private ones.

Market and long list: James Grant leads the mapping at the senior end, works the sectors where a General Counsel of this profile is actually found, and builds the long list from that map rather than from a list we already hold.

Research and profiles: I prepare the candidate research and the short profiles the consultants circulate, each drawn by current role rather than by name, so they are clean enough to drop into a slate.
Logistics: I keep the schedules, the client billing, and the meeting arrangements in order, so the search never goes quiet on the client or on a candidate while we are busy elsewhere.

blocks.text: First moves

The specification gates everything else, so that is where we start. This week Sandra Fuentes gets a first draft of the specification to Amy Alvarez, and I would like James Grant to open the market map in parallel, so we are not idle while the client reads. I will set a standing weekly check-in for the three of us and arrange a first calibration call once the draft is in the client's hands. If anyone sees a reason this plan will not hold, say so now, before the search is underway.

A word on how we will keep the thread orderly. This is a correspondence-heavy search, so the record matters as much as the calls, and I will hold the schedules, the notes, and the client billing in one place. Every candidate profile I circulate will carry a name at the top for questions, so nothing waits on a guess about who owns it. When something is delicate, it waits for a call rather than an email, and I will flag those to whichever of you owns the relationship.
That is the whole of it for now. Once the specification is agreed, the market work begins in earnest, and the memo after this one will be about candidates rather than plan.

To: Amy Alvarez
Cc: James Grant; Sandra Fuentes
Hi Amy,

A short update before our next call. The search for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} is moving on schedule, and I wanted you to have the shape of it in writing. James Grant has the market map nearly closed, and I have good early research on the seats we most want to reach. We are still at the stage of building the field rather than narrowing it, which is where a search of this kind should be at this point.

Two things would help from your side. First, a short read from the Howard, Carlson and Tran board on the two priorities we flagged in the draft specification, so I am not researching against a brief that has quietly shifted. Second, a note of any names inside your own network you would want us to include or to avoid. The candidate profiles I prepare will reach your committee under my name, Nicole Donovan, so please send any questions on them straight to me.

On timing, we are comfortably inside the window we set at the start. Once the map is closed this week, I will send a proposed date for our first proper review of where the field is heading, and we can fit it around your calendar rather than ours.
Regards
Meeting Minutes: General Counsel Search for Howard, Carlson and Tran

These minutes record our working session on the General Counsel search for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}, held to take stock of the field and to agree how the next stretch should run. The short version is that the search is where it should be: the specification is settled, the market map is largely built, and we are beginning to test our first real prospects. What follows is the detail behind that.
Present

items: Sandra Fuentes, Principal
James Grant, Principal
Nicole Donovan, Research Associate
Amy Alvarez, General Manager, Howard, Carlson and Tran

blocks.text: Where the search stands

We began with a recap of the field. James Grant walked the group through the map he has built at the senior end of the market, and we agreed it now covers the sectors where a General Counsel of this profile is genuinely to be found. Nicole Donovan has drawn early research on the seats we most want to reach, each described by current role rather than by name, which is how we will keep the whole field until both sides are ready to meet.

Two prospects are worth a closer look already, and we discussed each by their current seat: the deputy general counsel of a listed manufacturer, and the general counsel of a regional health system. Neither has been approached in a way that commits them, and we were careful to note that the field is still being built rather than narrowed. Amy Alvarez asked good questions about how we would test for the partner-to-leadership qualities the client cares most about, and we agreed those questions belong in the assessment rather than the first approach.
What the client needs from us

Amy Alvarez set the context plainly before making her one request. The board would like to see how a candidate has behaved when the business was under real pressure, not only how they present in a room. She asked, therefore, that our profiles carry a short, concrete account of judgment under strain for each person we bring forward. We agreed that Nicole Donovan will fold that into the profile format, and that James Grant will weigh it directly in his read of the finalists.
What we agreed to do next

rows: Close the remaining gaps in the market map and open first, uncommitting approaches to the strongest seats
Add a short account of judgment under pressure to the candidate profile format and update the drawn profiles to match
Confirm the assessment questions with the client and hold the relationship steady on both sides
Share any internal names the board would want included or avoided, and confirm the review cadence with her leadership

blocks.text: Our one priority before we next meet is to move the two leading prospects from names on a map into real conversations, without committing either side too early. Everything after that, including when a slate reaches the committee, follows from how those first approaches land.
Status Report: General Counsel Search for Howard, Carlson and Tran

Prepared for the client executive by Nicole Donovan, Research Associate. The search for {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} is on schedule and on budget at its midpoint. The field is built, the first prospects are in real conversations, and we expect to move from a broad field toward a short slate over the coming weeks. This report sets out what we finished in the last period, what comes next, where the budget sits, and the risks we are watching.
Where things stand

The specification is agreed and has held steady since kickoff, which is the main reason the search has stayed orderly. James Grant has completed the market map at the senior end, covering the sectors where a General Counsel of this profile is genuinely found rather than only the sectors that are easy to reach. Sandra Fuentes owns the client relationship and will own the assessment as the field narrows. We are squarely at the midpoint of the work: past the building of the field, and not yet at finalists and references. Nothing on the account is behind, and nothing has surprised us.
What we completed this period
The period's work went to closing the field and sharpening how we describe it.

items: Completed the market map at the senior end and confirmed it reaches the sectors where a General Counsel of this profile is actually found, rather than only the obvious ones.
Opened first, uncommitting approaches to the strongest prospects. Each is held by current role rather than by name, in keeping with how the client asked us to handle the field.

Revised the candidate profile format at the client's request to carry a short, concrete account of judgment under pressure, and updated the profiles already drawn so the whole field is described on the same terms.
Held the standing weekly review with the team, and kept the client's questions routed to a single point on our side so nothing was answered twice or missed.

blocks.text: What comes next
The next period turns from building the field to testing it.

items: Move the leading prospects from first approaches into full assessment, testing directly for the partner-to-leadership qualities the client cares most about rather than for presentation alone.
Begin the groundwork for references discreetly, arranging it so that no inquiry reaches a prospect's current employer.
Bring Sandra Fuentes's read of the client relationship and James Grant's judgment on the senior market together into a short slate, framed by fit and evidence rather than by name.
Propose a date for the first committee review of the field once the assessments are in hand, fitted around the client's calendar.

blocks.text: Budget

The engagement runs to the fixed professional fee of {{fact:f:E-2019-001.fee}}, agreed at the outset and unchanged since. We remain comfortably within it at the midpoint. Because the fee is fixed rather than tied to a candidate's eventual pay, the cost of the search does not move as the search does, and the client carries no surprise at the end. There are no expenses outstanding beyond the ordinary, and nothing unusual that we have not already flagged.
Risks and what we are watching
Three risks are worth naming, none of them pressing, all of them managed.

items: Availability: the strongest prospects are not looking, so a leading candidate could step back late. We keep more than one prospect warm to hold against it.
Brief drift: a specification can quietly shift as a board begins to picture candidates. We reconfirm the two priorities at each review to keep the search aimed at one brief.
Confidentiality: a General Counsel search touches sensitive ground. We describe candidates by their seat and hold names until both sides are ready, which slows nothing and protects everyone.

blocks.text: The single thing to watch between now and the next report is how the first assessments land. They will tell us whether the leading prospects hold up against the qualities the client cares most about, or whether we lean harder on the next names in the field. Once they are in, the field should resolve quickly toward a slate, and I will propose a review date the moment it does.
